Days after launching its username reservation system, WhatsApp is now beginning to roll out the full feature to select users. Here's what you need to know.

WhatsApp begins activating reserved usernames

Last month, WhatsApp introduced a username reservation system, allowing users to claim a unique handle before the full feature officially launches.

Users can claim their username by going to Settings > Account > Username, and can choose whether to allow anyone who knows it to contact them, or require new contacts to enter a four-digit PIN code in addition to the username.

When the chosen username matches an existing account on other Meta platforms such as Facebook or Instagram, users may need to verify they control that account. The move aims to prevent abuse of high-profile usernames and the potential for impersonation scams.

According to WABetaInfo, WhatsApp is now beginning to activate reserved usernames for a small number of accounts.

Users included in this initial rollout will now see a banner at the top of their chat list informing them that their username is active and can be shared with new contacts.

The report says the feature is rolling out simultaneously to beta testers and users on the stable version of WhatsApp, but emphasizes that it currently appears to cover only a "very small number of users."

To check whether your account has access to the feature, look for a banner at the top of your chat list, or head to the Username section in your profile settings. It will indicate whether your username is active, or display the message "Username coming soon—you'll be notified when it's ready."
